name: Anglian Water's Thriving Communities Fund
summary: Grants of £5,000 to £100,000 for non-profits in the Anglian Water region delivering physical improvements to the natural water environment, such as habitat restoration, river works and wetland creation, alongside community engagement.

geography.label: Anglian Water region (East of England and Hartlepool)

steps: EOI over £50k, or single-stage application at £5k–£50k

eligibility.rule: Have a track record of successful delivery
Own the land or hold a lease with 25 years remaining for major capital work
Major capital work: permission before applying. Smaller projects: expect it within 2 months of the deadline.
Submit no more than one application in the same round
Not seek repeat funding for work substantially funded by Anglian Water
Deliver physical interventions or capital work benefiting the natural water environment
Deliver social benefits through active community engagement with the local natural water environment.
Apply only if you have not already secured funding from this fund in the same year.

documents: Past-year accounts, or an income and expenditure record for small unincorporated or new groups
Bank statement or paying-in slip from the past three months
Three quotes for capital items or equipment over £500, if applicable
CICs: CIC 36 if registered in the past 12 months, otherwise latest CIC 34
Co-ops and community benefit societies: FCA registration in first 12 months, otherwise latest AR30
Evidence of a long-term lease, if the organisation does not own the land or building
List of three independent committee members, trustees or directors, and two independent cheque signatories

calls.label: Single-stage applications (£5,000 to £50,000), deadline 1 February 2027

status.quote: Applications reopen 2nd November with a submission deadline of 1st February 2027 (11.59 ie midday).

deadline.quote: Applications reopen 2nd November with a submission deadline of 1st February 2027 (11.59 ie midday).

calls.note: Route for grants up to £50,000; larger grants go through an expression of interest first.

administered_by.quote: This programme is managed by Cambridgeshire Community Foundation on behalf of Anglian Water.

applicant_types.quote: Applications are sought from non-profit organisations in the Anglian Water region with a track record of successful delivery.

geography.quote: supplies water and water recycling services to more than six million domestic and business customers in the East of England and Hartlepool

access.quote: Applications of £5,000 - £50,000 can submit a single stage application using the link below.

co_finance_required.quote: At the moment there is no fixed proportion of other funding required

consortium_required.quote: Projects can apply as a partnership, but the lead partner which submits the application must meet our not-for-profit requirements

effort.quote: Applications reopen 2nd November with a submission deadline of 1st February 2027 (11.59 ie midday).
EOI applications which are selected to go forward to the second stage will receive an invitation at the beginning of December, with a deadline of 1st February 2027.
Applications for grants over £50,000 should complete an Expression of Interest (EOI) form using the link below. EOI applications re-open 1st September with a submission deadline of 16th October.

eligibility.quote: Applications are sought from non-profit organisations in the Anglian Water region with a track record of successful delivery.
For projects involving major capital work, the applicant must own the land or hold a minimum lease of 25 years unexpired term.

Yes, for major capital projects you must have planning permission in place before you apply. For smaller projects you may apply if you expect to receive planning permission within 2 months of the submission deadline.
You should not submit more than one application for consideration at the same round.
Projects which have previously received substantial amounts from Anglian Water for the same or similar work
This means projects must deliver physical interventions or capital work that makes a positive difference to the natural water environment.

IN ADDITION to the main focus on physical improvements to the natural water environment, projects must deliver social benefits related to active community engagement with the local natural water environment.

You may submit an application to a succeeding round if the initial application was not awarded funding, but please do not submit a second application within the same year if the first was awarded funding.

after_award.quote: Around a month after the end of the project, grants recipients are required to complete an end-of-project reporting form online.

documents.quote: A signed governing document specific to your organisation, such as articles of association or a constitution, which must confirm that you are operating not for profit.

Accounts for the past year. If you are a small unincorporated group, we will accept an income and expenditure document or something similar. If your organisation is less than a year old, please provide a list of your income and expenditure to date. A recent bank statement or paying-in slip, from the last 3 months, to verify your organisation's banking details.

If you are applying for a grant to purchase capital items or equipment which would cost over £500, we require three different quotes. If you are a community interest company, we require your CIC 36 form (if you have registered as a CIC in the last 12 months), or your latest CIC 34 Annual Report (if you have been registered as a CIC for over 12 months).

If you are a co-operative or a community benefit society, we require your registration form submitted to the Financial Conduct Authority (if you have registered in the last 12 months) or a copy of your most recent AR30 form (if you have been registered for more than 12 months).
If you are looking for funding towards a building or land that your organisation does not own, we will need to see evidence of a long-term lease.

Names of three independent/unconnected management committee members/trustees/directors. To ensure your organisation has good governance and fair decision-making, we ask that management committee members/trustees/directors are independent/unconnected. We also require the names of two cheque signatories
